description: Source-lore pass 14 imports purpose-based vessel modifications, ship weapons, shipyards, upgrade economics, and port inspections.

entries.title: Airship Modifications
entries.summary: Construction yards reshape vessels around a single dominant mission such as passengers, cargo, scouting, combat, support, exploration, research, smuggling, or luxury.
body: Purpose-based modifications are major structural overhauls rather than minor accessories. They redistribute internal space, hull strength, engines, crew stations, weapons, stores, and specialized facilities so a vessel can excel at one role.

A ship supports only one purpose modification at a time because their structural and operational requirements conflict. Changing purpose requires substantial redesign and rebuilding, with cost increasing sharply by vessel class and shipyard capability.
Modification choices include [[passenger-liner-modification|passenger liner]], cargo hauler, scout, combat line, support, explorer, dreadnought, research, smuggler, and luxury configurations.

sections.heading: Legacy Upgrade Economy
body: The source gives class-based modification fees from Jetties through Dreadnoughts, resource costs, construction times, size restrictions, and numerical effects. These require conversion.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Putting all the pieces together / Purpose-Based Ship Modifications

entries.title: Passenger Liner Modification
entries.summary: Expanded cabins, stabilizers, entertainment spaces, and evacuation systems turn a vessel toward safe comfortable passenger service.
body: Passenger-liner conversion creates luxurious quarters, smooth-flight stabilizers, observation decks, dining halls, lounges, lifeboat pods, and emergency gliders.
The design carries more noncombatants in greater comfort but sacrifices weapons and freight space, requires additional maintenance, and handles poorly in combat.

sections.heading: Legacy Effects
body: The source adds passenger capacity and environmental comfort while penalizing combat maneuvering. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Cargo Hauler Modification
entries.summary: Expanded reinforced holds and mechanical loading rigs maximize freight capacity at the cost of speed, maneuverability, and armament.
body: Cargo-hauler conversion installs enlarged holds, cranes, mechanical arms, and stronger frames capable of bearing heavy loads.
It is a trade and supply configuration first: additional freight comes at the expense of combat readiness and flight performance.

sections.heading: Legacy Effects
body: The source increases cargo by fifty percent, reduces speed, and penalizes combat initiative. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Scout Vessel Modification
entries.summary: Light hulls, enhanced optics, scanners, noise damping, and smoke dispensers produce fast reconnaissance craft with little armor or cargo.
body: Scout conversion strips weight and installs superior observation and concealment systems. It is intended to discover routes, threats, targets, and anomalies before heavier ships arrive.
The gains in speed, perception, and stealth require minimal armor, freight, and passenger space.

sections.heading: Legacy Effects
body: The source increases speed and airborne perception while weakening damage resistance. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Combat Line Vessel Modification
entries.summary: Reinforced hulls, additional weapon platforms, and ammunition stores prepare a vessel for sustained front-line fighting.
body: Combat-line conversion adds armor plating, mounted-weapon positions, and enlarged ammunition stores. It transforms internal volume and structural support around surviving and delivering sustained fire.
The vessel becomes slower, less agile, and more expensive to maintain.

sections.heading: Legacy Effects
body: The source increases armor and mounted-weapon accuracy while reducing speed. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Support Vessel Modification
entries.summary: Repair bays, medical facilities, and supply stores allow a lightly armed vessel to sustain allied ships and crews.
body: Support conversion installs field-repair tools, magical maintenance devices, medical stations, and reserves of food, water, parts, and energy.
Such ships stabilize wounded crews and damaged vessels but depend on escorts because their own combat power and hull allocation are limited.

sections.heading: Legacy Effects
body: The source grants ship repair and automatic casualty stabilization while reducing maximum hull integrity. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Explorer Vessel Modification
entries.summary: Advanced charts, magical compasses, algae farms, purification systems, efficient engines, and survey tools support long voyages into unknown skies.
body: Explorer conversion makes a vessel self-sustaining and observant. Navigation archives, [[skycompass|magical compasses]], food cultivation, water purification, efficient propulsion, and anomaly-survey equipment reduce dependence on established ports.
The result is broadly capable but neither a dedicated warship nor a maximum-capacity freighter.

sections.heading: Legacy Effects
body: The source improves navigation, fuel efficiency, reserves, and hazard detection. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Dreadnought Modification
entries.summary: Fortified hulls, immense artillery, and siege systems convert a large vessel into a slow resource-hungry engine of destruction.
body: Dreadnought conversion devotes the ship to maximum armor and firepower. Fortified structures carry massive cannon or arcane artillery and support prolonged assaults against other great vessels, fortifications, or cities.
The configuration is extremely slow and cumbersome and requires extraordinary crews, ammunition, maintenance, and supply.

sections.heading: Legacy Effects
body: The source substantially increases armor and mounted-weapon damage while sharply reducing speed. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Research Vessel Modification
entries.summary: Arcane laboratories, specimen chambers, and advanced sensors turn a fragile vessel into a platform for magical and scientific study.
body: Research conversion installs laboratories, alchemical facilities, secure specimen storage, and sensors for magical auras, elemental events, creatures, and anomalies.
The specialized rooms consume space and structural capacity that would otherwise support armor or weapons.

sections.heading: Legacy Effects
body: The source improves Arcana and Nature work, permits safer anomaly storage, and reduces armor. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Smuggler's Vessel Modification
entries.summary: Hidden compartments, speed boosters, and camouflage systems prepare a lightly armed vessel for contraband and escape.
body: Smuggler conversion conceals freight, masks the hull against the sky, and reserves propulsion for rapid flight from inspection or pursuit.
Its hidden spaces reduce legitimate cargo capacity, and weight saved for speed and concealment leaves the vessel vulnerable if caught.

sections.heading: Legacy Effects
body: The source improves deception and speed while weakening resistance to damage. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Luxury Vessel Modification
entries.summary: Ornate interiors, banquet halls, theaters, magical performance spaces, and elite staff create a floating palace.
body: Luxury conversion turns a vessel into a status symbol for nobles, dignitaries, and wealthy travelers. High-end materials, lavish rooms, entertainment halls, and specialist servants dominate its design.
The floating palace excels at hospitality and influence but carries little freight or weaponry and moves slowly.

sections.heading: Legacy Effects
body: The source improves social checks with dignitaries and wealthy people while reducing speed. Conversion is required.

entries.title: Ship-Based Weapons
entries.summary: Airship weapons range from rail crossbows and dart launchers to broadside cannon, spinal behemoth guns, Skybreaker ballistas, and cataclysmic batteries.
body: Ship weapons operate on a scale beyond personal arms. The source treats ordinary character weapons as unable to damage vessels meaningfully, while ship-mounted guns are devastating against people and smaller creatures.

Light systems include rail crossbows, pneumatic dart shooters, and mini-turrets. Medium systems include light cannon, heavy crossbows, and deck ballistas. Heavy and massive systems include broadside batteries, spinal behemoth cannon, Skybreaker ballistas, and dreadnought-scale cataclysmic guns.

A weapon installation includes reinforced mounts, aiming mechanisms, ammunition magazines, power or powder systems, crew stations, training, maintenance, and reload labor. Larger weapons require more operators and become slower and less accurate when undermanned.

Ammunition cost and complexity rise sharply with scale. Heavy rounds consume steel, explosives, magical materials, specialized powder, and custom labor, making every major engagement an economic event as well as a battle.

sections.heading: Legacy Weapon Tables
body: The source maps weapons to all ten vessel classes and provides damage dice, range, reload time, installation prices, ammunition prices, crew requirements, and penalties for missing operators. These values require conversion.

entries.title: Shipyards of Kaysender
entries.summary: Shipyards range from tiny workbenches to imperial industrial complexes capable of building dreadnoughts, legendary ships, and superweapons.
body: Shipyard capability determines which vessels can be built, repaired, or modified. Small workbenches and docks handle Jetties, Scutters, and routine maintenance; private and regional yards build Corvettes, Frigates, and Cruisers; industrial, national, grand, and imperial yards support the largest military and arcane construction.

Higher tiers require progressively larger sites, more wood and metal, cloth, copper, glass, enchanted gems, rare or mythical materials, mechanized cranes, foundries, arcane workshops, storage, fuel systems, architects, engineers, craftspeople, laborers, and security.

Advanced yards shorten construction time and permit specialized cores, engines, military systems, and major redesigns. Their value also attracts piracy, theft, espionage, sabotage, and rival political pressure.

sections.heading: Legacy Shipyard Tables
body: The source defines six rating categories and a ten-level construction ladder with gold costs, area, material units, supplies, personnel, vessel limits, upgrade times, and resource requirements. These values require conversion.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Shipyard Rating System and Requirements / Shipyard Construction and Requirements

entries.title: Ship Inspections and Ownership Validation
entries.summary: Major ports inspect hulls, safety equipment, cargo, passengers, manifests, and ownership deeds, with foreign politics determining whether a vessel is admitted, delayed, fined, seized, or contested.
body: Major ports regulate incoming ships, especially Corvettes and larger vessels. Officials examine hull integrity, firefighting and rescue equipment, cargo, contraband, passenger manifests, and the crew's intentions before granting docking rights.

Captains must present a deed of ownership and legal registration. Foreign deeds may be rejected when nations are rivals or at war, creating seizure, quarantine, ownership disputes, cargo claims, delays, or demands for political influence and bribery.

Theocratic and monarchic ports emphasize loyalty; free cities use formal vetting; merchant states often favor trade value; pirate havens may ignore documents and recognize only force or negotiated allegiance.

Failed inspection can bring repair holds, fines, confiscation, imprisonment, political hostage-taking, or forced sale of cargo and vessel. Documentation is therefore as necessary to air travel as fuel and water.

sourceRefs.outlineTitle: Ship Inspections and Ownership Validation in Major Ports
